title: Yang–Mills and the Mass Gap over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The lattice determinations of $m(0^{++})/\sig$ for $\SU(3)$: the $r_0$ route with two inputs, $3.70(6)=5.73(9)\times0.6462(30)$ and $3.63(10)=4.21(11)/1.160(6)$, and the direct continuum extrapolation $3.405(21)$, a spread of $9\,\%$; $T_c/\sig=0.6462(30)$ ($\SU(3)$), $0.7091(36)$ ($\SU(2)$); the $r_0$ masses of $0^{++}$, $2^{++}$, $0^{-+}$ and $0^{++*}$.

rows.label: A2

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The strong coupling at two laboratory scales, $\alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1180(9)$ and $\alpha_s(m_\tau)=0.312(15)$, with the thresholds $M_Z$, $m_b$ and $m_\tau$.

rows.label: A5

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Four results of the framework: time is the drive (a theorem), mass is winding rate with masslessness as drive-invariance, confinement is the wrap of $\Om$-hard quark residues into exact hadron residues, and the gauge sector has one $\Om$-hard scale.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: Wilson's lattice gauge theory: the plaquette action on the hypercubic lattice, its strong-coupling character expansion, and the area law $W(A)=c_3^{A}$ at strong coupling, whose chart reading is the tension $a^{2}\sigma=-\ln c_3$ in lattice units, within the expansion's convergence.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: Two results of the interactions paper: the character lift (near the identity the frame's character equals the compact group's, to the stated order) and the order $\gcdop(3,q+1)$ of the centre of $\SU(3,\F_q)$.

rows.label: A9
rows.predicate: Steinberg's restriction theorem: for the finite frame and tensor degrees small compared with $q$, the invariants of $\mathbf3^{\otimes a}\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}^{\otimes b}$ are the algebraic group's, hence the compact multiplicities; verified by enumeration on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ over $\F_4$ to degree four (C9).

rows.label: A10

rows.label: A11

blocks.title: The finite theory and its readings

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A registration of a state by its frame is a line of the state's space that every frame element maps to itself; the residue is the number of such lines: photon $2$ (the split torus on the plane), gluon $0$ (the colour frame on the adjoint), baryon $1$, meson $1$, glueball $1$. Falsifier: a registered state of residue $0$.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: [chart] The chart's scale is read on the drive: a registered scale is a nonzero element $w$ of the Subject, two scales differ by the power $n$ with $\gen^{n}=w_2/w_1$, and the chart's $\ln(\mu_2/\mu_1)$ is read as $n\ln\gen$. The registration $\mu\mapsto w$ is the quantum paper's readout, not computed here.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The finite theory is the transfer form of lattice gauge theory on the substrate: the $\SU(3,\FOm)$ connection on the Subject's cells, the drive as the time step, the action in $\Z[\zeta_M]$ with the framed-rational readout. Its chart objects are the weight $e^{-\beta S}$ with real $\beta$, the wrap operator of C8 and the scale of B2.

blocks.title: The registrations, the sub-horizon tower and the tension

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate:
The non-split torus has no shell eigenvalue. For every frame of the totality a norm-one element $a+b\sqrt
u$ with $b

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The residue series closes with the glueball. On the $216$ elements of $\SU(3,\F_2)$ over $\F_4$ (no nontrivial character over $\F_4$) the adjoint action fixes no nonzero traceless matrix (gluon $0$), the determinant is the one invariant of $\Lambda^{3}$ (baryon $1$), and the commutants of the fundamental and the adjoint are one-dimensional (meson $1$, glueball $1$).

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: The drive exponent. On every shell of the totality the powers of the drive permute the nonzero elements: each winding rate has one exponent below $\p-1$, and exponents add modulo $\p-1$ --- the discrete logarithm on the shell. The ledger file decides it on the Subjects and the sweep.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
C1.doc: 46:C1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the non-split torus fixes no line of the shell plane, and the torus fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the non-split torus, is never registered alone.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.scalar_of_im_zero
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the two scalars `±1` are the only norm-one elements with `b = 0`: `a² = 1` forces `a = ±1`.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.split_fixed_lines
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the split torus `diag(g, g⁻¹)` fixes exactly the two coordinate lines of the projective line: a point `[x : y]` is fixed iff `g x · y = x · g⁻¹ y`, i.e. `(g² − 1) x y = 0`, i.e. `x y = 0` since `g² ≠ 1` (the drive is primitive of order `p − 1 > 2`). The photon's two helicities, residue `2`.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.centre_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the arithmetic of the centre's order formula. Given that the centre of `SU(3, 𝔽_q)` is the norm-one cube roots of unity, `gcd(3, q + 1)` of them (27-fields Proposition su3, imported, not proved here), on every shell of the sweep below `200`, `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` gives `Z₃` and `q ≡ 1 (mod 12)` the trivial centre, and the admissible residue `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is exactly `q ≡ 1 (mod 4)` (a shell) with `q ≡ 2 (mod 3)` (the triality centre). Kernel-decided over the range, so that no library lemma on `gcd` or `%` (which carry `propext`) enters.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.lab_centres
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the laboratory pairs: the Carriers `233`, `30089`, `2408561` carry the centre `Z₃`; of the Subjects, `173` does and `13`, `1549` do not.

C3.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
C3.doc: 46:C3 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the colour triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimirs
C4.doc: 46:C4 — the Casimirs of the colour frame with denominators cleared: `2N C_F = N² − 1` gives `6 C_F = 8` (`C_F = 4/3`), `C_A = N = 3`, `2 T_F = 1`, and `C_A / C_F = 2N² / (N² − 1)` gives `8 (C_A/C_F) = 18` (`9/4`).

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_pos
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ > 0` for every `n_f ≤ 16` (the sign the chart calls asymptotic freedom, for the matter content `n_f ≤ 16`).

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_neg
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ < 0` for every `n_f` from `17` to `200` (a bounded sweep, kernel-decided).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent
C6.doc: 46:C6 — every winding rate `w ≠ 0` is one power of the drive: `w = gⁿ` for some `n < p − 1` (the discrete logarithm of 26-pnp, `FrameCore.eq_pow_of_ne_zero`).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent_add
C6.doc: 46:C6 — the exponent of a product is the sum of the exponents, read modulo `p − 1`.

C9.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_two_sheets
C9.doc: 46:C9 — the two multiplicity identities of the adjoint wrap: the `β¹` coefficient of the adjoint plaquette coefficient vanishes (`E[χ²χ̄] + E[χχ̄²] − E[χ] − E[χ̄] = 0`, no singlet in `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛` or `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛̄`), and `4 E[(χχ̄ − 1)(Re χ)²] = 2` (`E[χ³χ̄] + 2E[χ²χ̄²] + E[χχ̄³] − E[χ²] − 2E[χχ̄] − E[χ̄²] = 2`), so `c₈ = β²/288 + …`, the square of `c₃`'s `β/18` up to the factor `9/8`: the adjoint wrap is two fundamental wraps. Stated on the sixfold multiplicities `moment6`.
